why_hard: The cause of the cardiomyopathy is never settled. One cardiologist favors ischemic and the EP favors non-ischemic, both hedged. GDMT is 2.6 months, so the answer flips on etiology.

pages.title: General cardiology note
lines: Office note 09/10/2026   Provider: Jonas Whitfield, MD
HFrEF dx 07/2026 (presented w/ edema/DOE). Long-standing DM2 and CKD 4 (eGFR 24).
Ischemic eval: invasive angiography deferred due to CKD 4 and contrast risk; pt also prefers to avoid cath. SPECT 07/30 w/ small fixed inferior defect, read as attenuation vs prior silent infarct.
Impression: Cardiomyopathy, etiology undetermined. I favor ischemic given long-standing diabetes and the fixed inferior defect, but cannot exclude a non-ischemic process.

pages.title: Nuclear stress test report
lines: Perfusion: small, mild-intensity fixed defect of the basal inferior wall. Breast and diaphragmatic attenuation present; attenuation-corrected images partially normalize the defect.
Impression: 1) Small fixed basal inferior defect - attenuation artifact vs small prior infarct; cannot exclude. 2) No ischemia. 3) Reduced LVEF.

pages.title: Echocardiogram report
lines: Global hypokinesis without clear regional pattern. LV dilated (LVIDd 6.3).
Mod functional MR. RV mildly reduced.
Impression: severe global LV dysfunction, LVEF 27%.

pages.title: EP consultation
lines: Sx: SOB walking room to room on bad days, usually half a block; no rest dyspnea. NYHA III.
Echo 9/17: LVEF 27%, global HK, no regional WMA.
No known MI. No PCI or CABG ever.
Assessment: Cardiomyopathy, likely non-ischemic given global pattern on echo; however ischemic etiology is not excluded without angiography (deferred for CKD 4).
Plan: pt and family want ICD before winter travel. SDM visit, then implant 10/20.
